evals.prompt: I just finished writing this little rate-limiter package for our internal gateway (token bucket, refills on a ticker goroutine, has a Wait(ctx) and an Allow() and a Close()). Can you write the tests for it before I send the PR? Package is in ./limiter
evals.expected_output: A small number of scenario tests exercising Allow/Wait/Close together from package limiter_test, concurrency and refill timing under testing/synctest (no sleeps), names claiming behavior (e.g. TestRefillGrantsBlockedWaiters), doc comments opening with the contract clause, possibly one Example; no per-function grain, no bug-hunt cases, no real-time flakiness.

evals.prompt: our new hire wrote tests for the config package (./config) and something feels off about them, can you review and fix? dont break anything, the suite is green
evals.expected_output: Identifies per-function grain, self-naming doc comments, a committed dev scaffold, an internals-reaching test, and a time.Sleep; consolidates into fewer contract scenarios, rewords comments to open with the contract clause, promotes the trivial case to an Example, deletes the scaffold with justification, keeps the suite green.

evals.prompt: add a test for the new ParseDurationOrDefault helper I added to internal/units (it falls back to the default on empty string, errors on garbage). quick one please, need to commit
evals.expected_output: Resists adding a lone TestParseDurationOrDefault bug-probe: either extends the package's existing scenario/table with rows for the new symbol, or adds a runnable Example if trivial, with a comment stating the documented fallback contract; checks the doc comment promises match what is asserted.
